children: is preparing to sell its controlling stake in used-car platform Aramis Group, with two investment banks mandated to work on a potential disposal, French publication L’Informé reported on Thursday.

owns 60.5% of Aramis’ capital and 67.4% of its voting rights, while the company’s founders own 17.9% and the remainder is publicly traded, according to L’Informé. Rothschild & Co. and Citi have been mandated for the potential sale.

Aramis, which was listed on Euronext Paris in 2021, currently has a market value of about €263 million, well below the roughly €1.9 billion valuation at its 2021 initial public offering, L’Informé said.
exit would mechanically result in Aramis leaving the stock market because the automaker’s stake exceeds the 30% threshold that triggers a mandatory tender offer, according to the report.

The potential sale comes as Aramis faces a weaker 2026. Sales declined more than 6% in the first nine months to €1.6 billion, while revenue from refurbished vehicles fell almost 5% and sales of pre-registered vehicles dropped 9%.

is seeking to focus on vehicle manufacturing and dispose of ancillary activities that are not sufficiently profitable, as the automaker faces competition from Chinese rivals and plans 60 billion euros of investment through 2030, it added.
Shares of the automaker were trading about 3.4% higher on Thursday.
